normalization: primitive reflecting hyperplanes modulo multiplication by units; totally positive units are squares

runs.local_norm_exhaustiveness_proof: For p=(-theta+2theta^2)=(t), N(p)=13, I(r) is O or p. If I(r)=p, then r0,...,r3 are in p and r4 is a p-adic unit, so q(r)=t*r4^2 mod p^2 and v_p(q)=1. If I(r)=O, reflection integrality forces v_p(q)=0. The inert prime (2) occurs to exponent at most one. Hence (q) is exactly one of (1),(2),p,2p; narrow class number one and squarehood of every totally positive unit give element representatives 1,2,t,2t up to unit scaling.
